# Model and source

* Citation: Hernandez Lozano I, Karch R, Bauer M, Blaickner M, Matsuda A,
  Wulkersdorfer B, Hacker M, Zeitlinger M, Langer O. Towards Improved
  Pharmacokinetic Models for the Analysis of Transporter-Mediated Hepatic
  Disposition of Drug Molecules with Positron Emission Tomography. AAPS J.
  2019;21(4):61.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1208/s12248-019-0323-0> (open access,
  PMC6488550, with an electronic supplementary document).

The paper analyses dynamic abdominal PET scans of the radiolabelled tyrosine
kinase inhibitor [11C]erlotinib in healthy volunteers. Tracer uptake from blood
into the liver and its excretion into bile are described by two compartment
models, each driven either by the sampled arterial blood curve (arterial input
function, AIF) or by a dual input function (DIF) that adds a mathematically
derived portal-vein curve. The four model variants were fitted to each subject
and scan separately; the paper reports the per-subject estimates and their mean
+/- SD for four scan conditions. nlmixr2lib packages one file per model variant:

| Model file | Structure | Input function | Source table |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HernandezLozano_2019_erlotinib_3c_aif` | 3C: liver tissue -> eBD/GB | AIF | Tables I, III |
| `HernandezLozano_2019_erlotinib_3c_dif` | 3C | DIF | Tables I, III |
| `HernandezLozano_2019_erlotinib_4c_aif` | 4C: hepatocytes -> intrahepatic bile duct -> eBD/GB | AIF | Tables II, IV |
| `HernandezLozano_2019_erlotinib_4c_dif` | 4C | DIF | Tables II, IV |

(eBD/GB: extrahepatic bile duct and gall bladder region of interest.) Each file
carries the four scan-condition mean parameter sets and selects one through
covariates:

| Scan condition | `STUDY_BAUER2018RIF` | `CONMED_ERLOTINIB` | `CONMED_RIFAMPICIN_SD` |
|---|---|---|---|
| [11C]erlotinib + erlotinib study, baseline | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| ... second scan 3 h after 300 mg oral erlotinib | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| [11C]erlotinib + rifampicin study, baseline | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| ... second scan after 600 mg i.v. rifampicin | 1 | 0 | 1 |

The blood input is not modelled: the arterial whole-blood radioactivity
concentration is supplied as the time-varying covariate `CP_ERLOTINIB_KBQML`
(kBq/mL), together with the liver volume `ORGVOL_LIVER` and the eBD/GB region
volume `ORGVOL_EBDGB` (mL). The outputs are the liver and eBD/GB region
concentrations `Cliver` and `Cgallbladder` (kBq/mL).

# Population

Twelve healthy volunteers in two studies of six (Methods, Data Sets), each
scanned twice about 7 days apart, previously published by Bauer et al. 2018
(Clin Pharmacol Ther 104:139, erlotinib study; Mol Pharm 15:4589, rifampicin
study). In the first study the second scan followed a 300 mg oral dose of
unlabelled erlotinib by 3 h; in the second it followed a 30-min i.v. infusion of
600 mg rifampicin. Arterial blood was sampled from the radial artery during each
90-min scan. Age, sex and body-size data are not reported in this paper. Each
subject and scan was fitted separately by weighted nonlinear least squares in
MATLAB, so the packaged parameters are means of individual estimates (a
two-stage summary), not population typical values.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 4C ODEs (hepatocytes, intrahepatic bile duct, eBD/GB) | `d/dt(liver) = k1 Xblood - (k2 + k3) liver`; `d/dt(bile_transit) = k3 liver - k5 bile_transit`; `d/dt(gallbladder) = k5 bile_transit` | Eqs. 4-6 |
| 3C ODEs (liver tissue, eBD/GB) | `d/dt(liver) = k1 Xblood - (k2 + k3) liver`; `d/dt(gallbladder) = k3 liver` | Eqs. 15-16 |
| Blood amount in the liver | `Xblood = Vb * V_liver * C_in` | Eq. 7 and text |
| Liver ROI concentration | `Vb * C_in + (X_hep + X_ih) / V_liver` (4C); `Vb * C_in + X_liv / V_liver` (3C) | Eqs. 11, 19 |
| eBD/GB ROI concentration | `X_eBD/GB / V_eBD/GB` | Eq. 12 |
| Portal-vein curve | convolution of `C_HA` with `h(t) = beta / (beta + t)^2` | Eqs. 1-2 |
| Dual input | `C_in = fHA * C_HA + fPV * C_PV` | Eq. 3 |
| `fvasc_liver` (Vb) | 0.25 (fixed) | Methods, after Eq. 7 and Eq. 11 |
| `fha`, `fpv` | 0.25, 0.75 (fixed) | Methods, after Eq. 3 |
| `kinf_liver_*` (k1), `keff_liver_*` (k2), `kbile_*` (k3) | four scan-condition means per model | Tables I-IV, Mean +/- SD rows |
| `ktr_bile_*` (k5) | four scan-condition means (4C only) | Tables II, IV |
| `beta_pv_*` (beta) | four scan-condition means (DIF only) | Tables I-IV |
| Residual error | none reported (weighted least squares, Eqs. 21-24); fixed to 0 | Methods |

## The packaged values are the printed means

Every rate constant in the four model files must equal the corresponding
printed mean. The check reads the `ini()` block of each model and compares it
cell by cell with the means table above.

```{r ini-equals-printed}
models <- c("3c_aif", "3c_dif", "4c_aif", "4c_dif")
stem <- function(m) paste0("HernandezLozano_2019_erlotinib_", m)
ini_name <- c(k1 = "kinf_liver", k2 = "keff_liver", k3 = "kbile", k5 = "ktr_bile", beta = "beta_pv")
cond_suffix <- c("erl.bl" = "erlbl", "erl.post" = "erlpost", "rif.bl" = "rifbl", "rif.post" = "rifpost")

ini_check <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) {
  ini <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(stem(m)))$iniDf
  cols <- grep(paste0("^", m, "_"), param_cols, value = TRUE)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(printed_mean)), function(i) {
    cond <- cond_suffix[[paste(printed_mean$study[i], printed_mean$scan[i], sep = ".")]]
    do.call(rbind, lapply(cols, function(cc) {
      p <- sub(paste0("^", m, "_"), "", cc)
      nm <- paste0(ini_name[[p]], "_", cond)
      data.frame(model = m, parameter = nm, printed = printed_mean[[cc]][i],
                 packaged = ini$est[ini$name == nm])
    }))
  }))
}))
nrow(ini_check)
stopifnot(
  nrow(ini_check) == 64,
  all(abs(ini_check$packaged - ini_check$printed) < 1e-12)
)
```

## The printed means agree with the per-subject rows

Recomputing each mean from the six per-subject estimates reproduces the printed
value to the third decimal (difference at most half a unit in the last printed
digit) in 63 of 64 cells. The exception is the 3C AIF k2 of the erlotinib-study
baseline scan: Table I prints 0.016, whereas its six subject rows (0.001,
0.032, 0.012, 0.010, 0.018, 0.010) average 0.0138. The packaged model keeps the
printed mean.

```{r means-vs-subjects}
recomputed <- subj |>
  group_by(study, scan) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(param_cols), mean), .groups = "drop")
diff_long <- recomputed |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(param_cols), names_to = "column", values_to = "recomputed") |>
  left_join(
    printed_mean |>
      select(-subject) |>
      pivot_longer(all_of(param_cols), names_to = "column", values_to = "printed"),
    by = c("study", "scan", "column")
  ) |>
  mutate(diff = recomputed - printed)
diff_long |>
  filter(abs(diff) > 0.00051) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
stopifnot(
  sum(abs(diff_long$diff) > 0.00051) == 1,
  with(
    diff_long[abs(diff_long$diff) > 0.00051, ],
    study == "erl" && scan == "bl" && column == "3c_aif_k2"
  )
)
```

## Eq. 13 holds with Vb = 0.25 and k1 acting on the blood amount

Eq. 13 defines the hepatic uptake clearance as `k1 * V_blood / w_body` with
`V_blood = Vb * V_liver`. Each subject's liver volume per kg can therefore be
back-calculated from any of the four models as `CL_H,uptake / (0.25 * k1)`. If
the packaged structure (k1 multiplying the blood AMOUNT, Vb = 0.25) is the one
the authors used, the four models must return the same liver volume for every
scan, since they share the subject's liver volume and weight.

```{r eq13-identity}
vw <- subj |>
  inner_join(cl, by = c("study", "scan", "subject"))
vliver_per_kg <- sapply(models, function(m) {
  vw[[paste0(m, "_up")]] / (0.25 * vw[[paste0(m, "_k1")]])
})
rownames(vliver_per_kg) <- paste(vw$study, vw$scan, vw$subject)
cv <- apply(vliver_per_kg, 1, function(z) sd(z) / mean(z))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(vliver_per_kg, `CV (%)` = 100 * cv, check.names = FALSE),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Liver volume per body weight (mL/kg) back-calculated from each model."
)
stopifnot(
  median(cv) < 0.02,
  # p12 after erlotinib, 3C DIF: Supplemental Table II prints CL_H,uptake = 12.437,
  # about half of what its k1 = 3.891 and its other three models imply (~22 mL/kg).
  sum(cv > 0.05) == 1,
  names(which(cv > 0.05)) == "erl post p12",
  abs(median(vliver_per_kg) - 22) < 1.5
)
```

The liver volumes cluster at `r round(median(vliver_per_kg), 1)` mL/kg (median),
a plausible adult liver volume per body weight for a volume computed from body
size (the paper cites Vauthey et al. 2002). This also gives a realistic
`ORGVOL_LIVER` for the simulations below: about 1650 mL for a 75 kg adult.

# A representative arterial input function

The per-subject arterial curves are not tabulated. Supplemental Fig. 15 plots the
sampled arterial curve (assumed equal to the hepatic-artery curve), the derived
portal-vein curve and the dual input for subject p30, whose estimated beta was
1.050 min (the 4C DIF fit of the scan after oral erlotinib, Table II). The
maintainers digitised all three curves from the 0-10 min inset (one value per
plotted sample) and the arterial tail from the main panel (10-47.5 min; beyond
48 min the arterial line is hidden under the other two). The tail beyond 47.5 min
is extrapolated log-linearly for the illustrative simulations only.

```{r aif}
fig15 <- data.frame(
  time = c(0, 0.354, 0.709, 1.063, 1.417, 1.772, 2.126, 2.48, 2.834, 3.189,
           3.543, 3.897, 4.252, 4.606, 4.96, 5.314, 5.669, 6.023, 6.377, 6.732,
           7.086, 7.44, 7.795, 8.149, 8.503, 8.858, 9.212, 9.566, 9.92, 10.275),
  ha = c(0, 57.5, 101.7, 47.1, 29.1, 21.52, 16.65, 14.82, 12.99, 11.16, 9.63,

         5.06, 4.76, 4.45, 4.45, 4.45, 4.45, 4.15),
  pv = c(0, 10.2, 26.5, 27.9, 25.5, 24.57, 21.83, 20, 18.78, 17.26, 15.73, 14.51,
         13.6, 12.68, 12.07, 11.16, 10.55, 10.24, 9.63, 9.63, 9.02, 8.72, 8.41,
         8.41, 8.11, 7.8, 7.8, 7.5, 7.2, 6.89),
  dif = c(0, 22.4, 45, 33.4, 27, 23.35, 20.3, 18.17, 16.65, 15.12, 13.9, 12.68,
          11.77, 10.85, 10.24, 9.63, 9.33, 9.02, 8.41, 8.11, 7.8, 7.5, 7.2, 7.2,
          7.2, 6.59, 6.59, 6.28, 5.98, 5.98)
)
fig15_tail <- data.frame(
  time = c(12.5, 15, 17.5, 20, 22.5, 25, 27.5, 30, 32.5, 35, 37.5, 40, 45, 47.5),
  ha = c(4.02, 3.65, 3.27, 2.91, 2.63, 2.55, 2.23, 2.18, 2.04, 1.82, 1.82, 1.82,
         1.45, 1.45)
)
tail_fit <- lm(log(ha) ~ time, data = fig15_tail)
extrap <- data.frame(time = seq(50, 95, by = 5))
extrap$ha <- exp(predict(tail_fit, extrap))
aif <- bind_rows(fig15[, c("time", "ha")], fig15_tail, extrap)
aif_fun <- approxfun(aif$time, aif$ha, rule = 2)

# The plotted dual input obeys Eq. 3 with fHA = 0.25 and fPV = 0.75.
dif_identity <- 0.25 * fig15$ha + 0.75 * fig15$pv - fig15$dif
stopifnot(max(abs(dif_identity)) < 1.2)

ggplot(aif, aes(time, ha)) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_point(data = bind_rows(fig15[, c("time", "ha")], fig15_tail), colour = "firebrick", size = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Arterial blood (kBq/mL)",
       title = "Digitised arterial input of subject p30 (Supplemental Fig. 15)")
```

# The portal-vein convolution

The DIF models evaluate the convolution of Eqs. 1-2 inside the ODE system. The
kernel `beta / (beta + t)^2` is a continuous mixture of exponentials,
`(1/beta) * integral u exp(-u) exp(-u t / beta) du`, so a trapezoid rule in
`log(u)` turns it into 14 exponential terms, each solved as one linear ODE
(`pvconv1` ... `pvconv14`).

```{r kernel-accuracy}
x_nodes <- -9:4
kernel_quad <- function(t, beta) {
  sapply(t, function(tt) sum(exp(2 * x_nodes - exp(x_nodes)) / beta * exp(-exp(x_nodes) * tt / beta)))
}
t_grid <- c(0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 45, 90, 120)
kernel_err <- sapply(c(0.5, 0.971, 1.05, 1.956, 2.5), function(b) {
  max(abs(kernel_quad(t_grid, b) / (b / (b + t_grid)^2) - 1))
})
round(kernel_err, 5)
stopifnot(max(kernel_err) < 0.005)
```

Solving the packaged 4C DIF model with p30's digitised arterial curve and
beta = 1.050 min must give the same portal-vein curve as a direct numerical
convolution of that arterial curve.

```{r pv-check}
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(aif$time[aif$time <= 90], seq(0, 90, by = 0.25))))
make_events <- function(study, erl, rif, vliver = 1650, vebdgb = 40) {
  data.frame(
    id = 1, time = obs_times, evid = 0, dvid = 1,
    CP_ERLOTINIB_KBQML = aif_fun(obs_times),
    ORGVOL_LIVER = vliver, ORGVOL_EBDGB = vebdgb,
    STUDY_BAUER2018RIF = study, CONMED_ERLOTINIB = erl, CONMED_RIFAMPICIN_SD = rif
  )
}
mod_4c_dif <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(stem("4c_dif")))
mod_p30 <- rxode2::ini(mod_4c_dif, beta_pv_erlpost = 1.050)
sim_pv <- rxSolve(mod_p30, make_events(0, 1, 0), returnType = "data.frame",
                  atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10)

direct_conv <- function(t, beta, dt = 0.001) {
  sapply(t, function(tt) {
    if (tt == 0) return(0)
    tau <- seq(0, tt, by = dt)
    y <- beta / (beta + tt - tau)^2 * aif_fun(tau)
    sum(y[-1] + y[-length(y)]) / 2 * dt
  })
}
pv_cmp <- data.frame(time = fig15$time) |>
  mutate(
    model_cpv = approx(sim_pv$time, sim_pv$cpv, time)$y,
    direct = direct_conv(time, 1.050),
    published = fig15$pv
  )
stopifnot(max(abs(pv_cmp$model_cpv - pv_cmp$direct)) < 0.01 * max(pv_cmp$direct))
knitr::kable(pv_cmp[c(2:8, 11, 16, 21, 30), ], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Portal-vein curve (kBq/mL) for p30, beta = 1.050 min.")
```

The packaged convolution matches the direct numerical integral to within 1% of
the peak. The published portal-vein curve of Supplemental Fig. 15 has the same
shape and timing: it peaks at the same sample, 1.06 min. It differs in detail,
though: its peak is about 17% lower (27.9 vs 33.5 kBq/mL) and from 3.5 to
10 min it runs 7-30% higher than the convolution of the plotted arterial curve
with the printed beta. The
authors' MATLAB discretisation of Eq. 1 is not published, and the digitised
arterial curve carries its own reading error, so this difference is documented
rather than tuned away.

```{r pv-plot}
pv_cmp |>
  select(time, `Packaged model` = model_cpv, `Published (Suppl. Fig. 15)` = published) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "source", values_to = "pv") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, pv, colour = source)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  geom_line(data = fig15, aes(time, ha), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey50", linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Concentration (kBq/mL)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Portal-vein input for p30 (dashed: arterial input)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Simulated liver and eBD/GB curves for the four scan conditions

The scan-condition means are summaries of individual fits, each obtained with
that subject's own arterial curve. To compare the four conditions on a common
footing, every model and condition below is driven by the same representative
input (p30's digitised arterial curve), with `ORGVOL_LIVER` = 1650 mL and an
illustrative `ORGVOL_EBDGB` of 40 mL (the eBD/GB volumes are not reported; the
eBD/GB concentration scales with `ORGVOL_LIVER / ORGVOL_EBDGB`).

```{r conditions}
conditions <- data.frame(
  condition = c("Erlotinib study: baseline", "Erlotinib study: after oral erlotinib",
                "Rifampicin study: baseline", "Rifampicin study: after i.v. rifampicin"),
  study = c(0, 0, 1, 1), erl = c(0, 1, 0, 0), rif = c(0, 0, 0, 1)
)
sims <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) {
  mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(stem(m)))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(conditions)), function(i) {
    s <- rxSolve(mod, make_events(conditions$study[i], conditions$erl[i], conditions$rif[i]),
                 returnType = "data.frame")
    data.frame(model = toupper(sub("_", " ", m)), condition = conditions$condition[i],
               time = s$time, Cliver = s$Cliver, Cgallbladder = s$Cgallbladder)
  }))
}))
sims$condition <- factor(sims$condition, levels = conditions$condition)

ggplot(sims, aes(time, Cliver, colour = condition)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Liver ROI (kBq/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
ggplot(sims, aes(time, Cgallbladder, colour = condition)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "eBD/GB ROI (kBq/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

The paper's main finding for the erlotinib study is a significant rise of k2
(liver-to-blood backflux) after oral erlotinib in every model, which lowers the
late liver signal for a given blood input. Driven by the same input, every model
reproduces that direction:

```{r direction}
late_liver <- sims |>
  filter(time >= 60, time <= 90) |>
  group_by(model, condition) |>
  summarise(mean_late_liver = mean(Cliver), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = mean_late_liver)
knitr::kable(late_liver, digits = 1,
             caption = "Mean liver ROI concentration, 60-90 min (kBq/mL).")
stopifnot(all(late_liver[["Erlotinib study: after oral erlotinib"]] <
                late_liver[["Erlotinib study: baseline"]]))
```

# Individual-subject check: p30 after oral erlotinib

Supplemental Fig. 15 belongs to the same subject and scan as the fitted liver
curves of Supplemental Fig. 5c (p30, scan after oral erlotinib). Substituting
p30's own estimates (Tables I-II) and the digitised arterial curve gives the
early liver peak, which is set by k1, Vb and the first two minutes of the input,
where the digitised curve is most reliable. The published peaks of the fitted
lines were digitised from Supplemental Fig. 5c.

```{r p30}
p30 <- list(
  "3c_aif" = c(kinf_liver_erlpost = 2.080, keff_liver_erlpost = 0.137, kbile_erlpost = 0.0001),
  "3c_dif" = c(kinf_liver_erlpost = 3.585, keff_liver_erlpost = 0.092, kbile_erlpost = 0.0002,
               beta_pv_erlpost = 2.154),
  "4c_aif" = c(kinf_liver_erlpost = 2.606, keff_liver_erlpost = 0.189, kbile_erlpost = 0.002,
               ktr_bile_erlpost = 0.003),
  "4c_dif" = c(kinf_liver_erlpost = 4.000, keff_liver_erlpost = 0.140, kbile_erlpost = 0.006,
               ktr_bile_erlpost = 0.002, beta_pv_erlpost = 1.050)
)
published_peak <- c("3c_aif" = NA, "3c_dif" = 48.4, "4c_aif" = 56.1, "4c_dif" = 55.3)
p30_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) {
  mod <- do.call(rxode2::ini, c(list(rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(stem(m)))), as.list(p30[[m]])))
  s <- rxSolve(mod, make_events(0, 1, 0), returnType = "data.frame")
  early <- s[s$time <= 15, ]
  data.frame(
    model = m,
    simulated_peak = max(early$Cliver),
    simulated_peak_time = early$time[which.max(early$Cliver)],
    published_peak = published_peak[[m]],
    simulated_88min = approx(s$time, s$Cliver, 88)$y
  )
}))
knitr::kable(p30_tab, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "p30 after oral erlotinib: liver ROI (kBq/mL).")
```

The 4C AIF model reaches its early peak within about 5% of the published
fitted line (`r round(p30_tab$simulated_peak[3], 1)` vs 56.1 kBq/mL at about
2 min); the 3C AIF line cannot be separated from the observed circles in the
figure. The DIF models peak later and higher than the published lines (3C DIF
`r round(p30_tab$simulated_peak[2], 1)` vs 48.4, 4C DIF
`r round(p30_tab$simulated_peak[4], 1)` vs 55.3 kBq/mL), and none of the four
reproduces the late plateau of about 21 kBq/mL. With p30's 4C AIF constants the
liver-to-blood ratio at quasi-equilibrium is about `k1 * Vb / (k2 + k3)` = 3.4, so
the published plateau needs a late arterial concentration of about 6 kBq/mL,
several times the 0.4-1.8 kBq/mL read from the plotted tail of Supplemental
Fig. 15 (20-90 min). Decay correction is one possible explanation: the paper
does not say whether the plotted input functions are decay-corrected, and
multiplying the 20-40 min tail by `exp(log(2) / 20.4 * t)` gives 5.7-7.1 kBq/mL.
These points are documented, not asserted; the whole-curve fits cannot be
reproduced without the per-subject arterial data.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Mean parameters, not population typical values.** Each subject and scan
  was fitted separately (weighted least squares in MATLAB); the packaged values
  are the printed means of the six individual estimates per condition. The
  model output for a mean parameter set is not the mean of the individual
  curves. The between-subject SDs are quoted in the `ini()` comments but no
  random effects are encoded.
* **Residual error.** The fits used weighted least squares with weights from
  the frame length and the 11C decay (Eqs. 22-24); no residual-error magnitude
  is reported, so `propSd_Cliver` and `propSd_Cgallbladder` are fixed to 0.
* **Arterial input as a covariate.** The radial-artery whole-blood curve is
  supplied as `CP_ERLOTINIB_KBQML` and interpolated linearly. It must be on the
  same decay-correction basis as the PET data being modelled.
* **Portal-vein convolution.** Eq. 1 is evaluated as a 14-term
  sum-of-exponentials quadrature of the Eq. 2 kernel (maximum relative kernel
  error below 0.5% for 0-120 min), solved as linear ODEs. The authors'
  discretisation is not published (see the portal-vein comparison above).
* **eBD/GB initial signal.** The printed equations start the eBD/GB amount at
  zero, but the fitted eBD/GB lines in Figs. 2 and 4 and Supplemental Figs. 1-12
  start at a non-zero concentration (about 35 kBq/mL at 2 min in Fig. 2b), which
  can differ between the four models (about 28 kBq/mL for the 4C and 45 kBq/mL
  for the 3C lines in the p30 baseline eBD/GB panel of Supplemental Fig. 5). The paper does not describe this offset, and the packaged models
  follow the printed equations. A user who needs it can set the initial eBD/GB
  amount through `rxSolve(..., inits = c(gallbladder = C0 * ORGVOL_EBDGB))`.
* **Volumes.** `ORGVOL_LIVER` was computed by the authors from body surface
  area (Vauthey 2002); the back-calculation above gives about 22 mL/kg.
  `ORGVOL_EBDGB` was derived from the PET images and is not reported. The liver
  ROI output does not depend on either volume; the eBD/GB output scales with
  their ratio.
* **Scan-condition covariates.** `STUDY_BAUER2018RIF` selects the cohort, and
  `CONMED_ERLOTINIB` / `CONMED_RIFAMPICIN_SD` select the second scan within it.
  Setting the second-scan indicator of the other study has no effect.
* **Errata found in the source tables.** Table I prints the 3C AIF baseline k2
  mean as 0.016, but its subject rows average 0.0138 (the printed value is kept).
  Supplemental Table II prints `CL_H,uptake` = 12.437 mL/min/kg for p12 (3C DIF,
  scan after erlotinib), about half of what its k1 implies (about 22 mL/kg x 0.25
  x 3.891). The hepatic efflux clearances of Supplemental Tables II and IV are
  derived quantities and are not part of the packaged models.
* **No NCA.** There is no dose event (the tracer enters through the measured
  blood curve) and the paper reports no non-compartmental parameters, so the
  checks above replace the usual PKNCA comparison.
